title: Quiz: The Markov Property and Transition Matrices

options: The process has no memory of any past states whatsoever
Future states depend only on the current state, not on the history of how you got there
All transition probabilities must be equal
The process always reaches a steady state
questions.explanation: Option (b) is precisely correct. Option (a) is subtly wrong: the current state is itself a past state that is retained — 'no memory of any past state' would mean the process ignores its current position too, which is not what a Markov chain does. The Markov property says the future depends on the present state only, not on the full history.

questions.text: In a transition probability matrix P, the entry P_{23} means:
options: The probability of going from state 3 to state 2 in one step
The probability of being in state 2 at time step 3
The probability of going from state 2 to state 3 in one step
The third power of the entry P_{2}
questions.explanation: The convention is always: row index = current state, column index = next state. So P_{23} = P[X_{n+1} = 3 | X_n = 2] — the one-step transition probability from state 2 to state 3. Option (a) reverses the direction. Options (b) and (d) are different concepts entirely.

questions.text: A stochastic matrix can have a row that sums to 0.99 due to rounding, and this is still a valid transition probability matrix.
questions.explanation: False. By definition, a stochastic matrix requires each row to sum to exactly 1. A row summing to 0.99 violates the axiom that the probabilities of all possible next states must sum to 1. In numerical computations, rows should be normalised to enforce this exactly; a discrepancy due to rounding indicates a modelling or coding error.

questions.text: In a time-homogeneous Markov chain, the notation P_{ij}^{(t)} = P_{ij} for all t means:
options: The transition probability changes with t, so we must track the superscript
The transition probability from state i to state j is the same regardless of when you make the transition
Time must be discrete for the chain to be valid
The transition matrix is a diagonal matrix
questions.explanation: Time-homogeneity means the one-step transition probabilities do not depend on the current time t — the same matrix P governs every step. This is a simplifying assumption (not always realistic) that makes analysis tractable. It says nothing about discrete vs. continuous time or about the matrix being diagonal.

questions.text: An absorbing state is one from which the process can never escape once entered.
questions.explanation: True. State i is absorbing if and only if P_{ii} = 1 (equivalently, P_{ij} = 0 for all j ≠ i). Once in an absorbing state, the chain stays there forever. Biological examples include death in a health model or fixation in a population genetics model.
